A.R. Yusuf
Vs.
The Commissioner of Taxes
full_judgment:
2. The applicant for the assessment year 1994-95 filed the wealth tax return under Wealth Tax Act, 1963 showing his house property valued at Tk. 17,35,706 and Tk. 5,07,200/- the municipal annual valuation and also filed statement of assets and liabilities. The Deputy Commissioner of Taxes asked the assessee applicant to file the tenancy agreement on the basis of which the house in question was let out, municipal assessment notice and the receipt showing payment of municipal tax, and accordingly the assessee produced all these papers before the Deputy Commissioner or Taxes. The Deputy Commissioner of Taxes determined and estimated the value of the house property of the assessee applicant on the basis of 12th times of the gross annual rental value of the house which stood at Tk. 79,20,000/-. The applicant has stated that in the past assessment years the assessing officer determined the value at Tk. 27,29,004/-, Tk. 30,70,004/-, 32,11,879/- and 34,20,000/-, respectively. For the assessment year 1995-96 the applicant filed Wealth Tax return showing the valuation of his house property at Tk. 17,35,706/- and for the assessment year 1996-97 the applicant filed similar return showing valuation of the house at Tk. 17,35,706/- and the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes estimated the value for both the years under assessment at Tk. 79,20,000/- for the purpose of imposing tax. 

 4. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances the applicant has referred to us the following question of law which is said to arise from the impugned judgment passed by the Taxes Appellate Tribunal for our decision. 

 The similar question has been formulated in other two reference applications relating to assessment years 1995-96 and 1996-97 for our answer. 

 5. It is contended by Mr. Ferojuddin Bhuiyan, the learned advocate for the applicant, that the Tribunal committed an error in law in not following the rule 8(3) of the Wealth Tax Rule, 1963 in determining the value of the house property of the assessee applicant. He has further contended that there are various modes of valuation for determining the value of the house property for the purpose of wealth tax and modes of valuation as envisaged in sub-rule (3) of rule 8 ought to have been applied by the Taxing authority. Mr. Bhuiyan has pointed out that rule 8(3) of the Wealth Tax Rules which was framed by the National Board of Revenue under section 46 of the Wealth Tax Act, 1963 had undergone changes from time to time and subsequently the said rule was amended by notification dated 4th May, 1982 and the proviso in the present form has been appended to sub-rule (3) of rule 8 of the Wealth Tax Rules, 1963 and the proviso as amended will although restrict the main sub-rule (3), but the assessing officer, the Deputy Commissioner of taxes, without resorting to sub-rule (3) can not estimate the value of the property equal to 12 times of the gross annual rental value of such property. It has further been pointed out by the learned Advocate that sub-rule (3) of rule 8 has again been amended and for the words twenty times the words fifteen times has been substituted by notification dated 30thJune, 1982 issued by the National board of Revenue. 

 6. It appears that the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes being the wealth tax assessing officer determined the value of the house property of the applicant at Tk. 79,29,000/- for all the years under assessment by resorting to the proviso appended to sub-rule (3) as it now stands is in the following terms:- 

 "Land and buildings- The value of lands and buildings shall be estimated with due regard to the nature and size of the property, the amenities available and the price prevailing for similar assets in the same locality or the neighborhood of the said locality; 

 Provided that the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes shall not except with the prior approval of the Inspecting Joint Commissioner of Taxes, estimate a value higher than a sum equal to fifteen times the gross annual rental value of such property. 

 Explanation-For the purposes of this sub-rule, "gross annual rental value" means the sum for which the property might reasonably be expected to let from year to year." 

 7. The value of assets is to be determined under the Wealth Tax Act 1963 according to the provision of section 7 of the Act which is as follows:- 

 "Section 7 (1)-The value of any assets, other than cash for the purpose of this act shall be estimated by the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes in accordance with the Rules made under section 46 of the Act. Pursuant to the provision of section 7 the rules were framed by the National Board of Revenue for carrying out the purposes of the Act. 

 "Provided that where the capital value of such property has been determined by the appropriate local Government authority for purposes of property taxation under the laws and regulations in force in the said locality, the Wealth Tax Officer shall adopt such capital value (as determined in the latest assessment) as the value of such property for purposes of assessment to wealth tax. 

 Provided further that where the capital value of such property has been so determined, the Wealth Tax Officer shall not, except with the prior approval of the Inspecting Assistant Commissioner of Wealth Tax, adopt a value higher than a sum equal to ten times the gross annual rental value of such property". 

 Before the first appellate authority the assessee 'claimed that the value should be estimated according to the municipal value as determined in the latest assessment. 

 These two provision have been deleted by S.R.O. No. 139-L/82 dated 4th May, 1982 and the present proviso which is stated above has been inserted with the explanation where in stead of the words "gross annual value", "gross annual rental value" has been inserted. 

 9. The Joint Commissioner of Taxes as it appears from the short order has upheld the order of the assessing officer without however considering the relevant provision as laid down in sub-rule (3) of rule 8 and also the power of the assessing officer to fix the valuation as provided under the proviso appended to the sub-rule. The Taxes Appellate Tribunal although has referred to sub-rule (3) and the provisos which were in force before coming into force of the amended proviso through the notification dated 4th May, 1982, but failed to apply the present provision with correct interpretation finding out the meaning and true legislative intent, and consequently wrongly upheld the order passed by the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes affirming the assessment order. 

 10. The cardinal principle and the mandatory provision in interpreting a section of particular statute or the rule framed there under is that the proviso controls and restricts the main section or the main rule, and proviso to a section or to a rules is to be regarded to have an overriding effect and control ever the whole section or the rule. Mr. Ferojuddin Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate, has contended that the value of the land and building for which the wealth tax is to be imposed shall be estimated firstly having regard to the nature and size of the property, the amenities  available and the price prevailing for similar assets in the same locality or the neighborhood of the said locality as per provision of sub-rule 3, but the assessing officer, the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes, without following the express provision as envisaged in that sub-rule estimated the value of the house property of the applicant according to the proviso which does not expressly restrict the other conditions in determining the value. 

 11. In the proviso it is seen that the language that has been used implies that the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes shall not estimate the value of land and building higher than a sum equal to fifteen times without the approval of the inspecting Joint Commissioner of Taxes. The word estimate connotes and it refers to the value to be determined with due regard to the nature and size of the property, the amenities available and the price prevailing for similar asset in the same locality or neighborhood of the said locality. In estimating the value of the property, having regard to the nature, size, amenities available and the price prevailing far similar assets in the same locality, if it does exceed the limit as mentioned in the proviso in that case approval of the Inspecting Joint Commissioner of Taxes is necessary. In the present proviso the provision of fifteen times has been inserted only for the purpose of obtaining prior persuasion of the higher authority, namely, Inspecting Joint Commissioner of Taxes: The proviso has not put any restriction on the power of the assessing officer to estimate the value in the manner as prescribed in the said sub-rule (3) in determining the valuation of the property and in doing so if it does exceed the sum which is equal to fifteen times the gross annual rental of such property in that case that value may he adopted for the purpose of imposing tax with the approval of the higher authority. But the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes in any case cannot follow the policy which has been incorporated in the proviso blindly and fix the sum multiplying the gross annual rental value by twelve times and fifteen times ignoring the provision of sub-rules (3). In explanation it has been stated that for the purpose of this sub-rule, gross annual rental value means .the sum for which the property might reasonably be expected the let from year to year. So this gross annual rental value is always subject to change, it may change from year to year; there is no certainty that the gross annual rental value will remain the same for all the years to come. In the instant case the applicant disclosed the yearly rental of the house at Tk. 6,60,000/- in his income tax return as bonafide annual rental and the assessing officer adopted that value and multiplied the sum by twelve times for the purpose of assessment of wealth tax, which is not permitted under sub rule (3) of rule 8 of the Wealth Tax Rules and the proviso thereof. 

 12. In the view we are of the opinion that the Taxes Appellate Tribunal was not justified at all in upholding the valuation of the house property of the assessee applicant without following sub rule 3 of Rule 8 of the Wealth Tax Rule. The question as raised is, therefore, answered in the negative and in favour of the assessee in all the 3 reference applications, But since the valuation has not been estimated according to the provision of sub rule (3) of rule 8 of the Wealth Tax Rules the matter is referred back to the Taxes Appellate Tribunal for determining the value is accordance with law and the observation made above, and in that case the Tribunal is at liberty to send the matter to the assessing officer to estimate the value in accordance with the provision of sub-rule (3).
